summary: Business Today rounds up social media reactions to Hamas' surprise coordinated attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, which led many to question the intelligence capability of Mossad. Commentators described it as a massive intelligence failure, while others speculated Mossad knew in advance and let it happen to justify retaliation. Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu declared Israel at war and laid out three objectives.
one_line: Social media users question Mossad's reputation after Hamas' unexpected large-scale attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, as Netanyahu declares war.
key_facts: Hamas carried out the biggest coordinated attack in Israel and captured some territory in southern Israel on October 7, 2023.
People were surprised less by the attack itself than by its scale, with Hamas gaining control of some military bases and soldiers.
Younis Tirawi, who reports on Palestinian affairs, said Hamas militants had taken over Sderot police HQ and armored vehicles in the town.
Journalist Rania Khalek said the strategic planning against "one of the most high-tech occupation and surveillance systems in the world" will be studied by many.
Tarik Cyril Amar said both Israel's intel and special forces training were areas where "Israel mythology will be very upset indeed."
User Mjoachim claimed the IDF lost an army base, a general was captured from his house, and Merkava MK4 tanks were captured and destroyed.
Management professor Dr Jaswant Gandhi called it a "great Mossad failure" and said India must keep its intelligence agencies duly greased and internecine conflict-proof.
Some users speculated Mossad knew about the attack but let Hamas proceed to give Israel a reason to launch a ferocious retaliation.
Netanyahu said Israel's first objective is to clear out hostile forces that infiltrated its territory and restore security to attacked communities.
Netanyahu's second objective is to exact an immense price from the enemy within the Gaza Strip, and the third is to reinforce other fronts so nobody joins the war.
Journalist Ben Muasya said Mossad is overrated and wondered whether the attack was a trap to justify heavy retaliation.
One user said knowing Mossad's proficiency, he found the idea of a "surprise attack" to be a willing lie on Netanyahu's part.
